newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russian sunseed exports to dry up in May.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russian sunseed exports to dry up in May.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union. RUSSIA'S SUNSEED EXPORTS TO BE NEARLY EXHAUSTED BY END MAY
MOSCOW, April 7 - It is very likely that domestic oilers will soon face a shortage of sunseeds for processing.
Since December 1996, Russia's sunseed exports have been rapidly declining.
The drop reflects reduced sunseed output (2.75 million tonnes) last year, compared to 4.2 million tonnes in 1995, combined with shipments over October-December 1996.
As a result, SovEcon expects that Russia's sunseed exports will sharply decline in April and are likely to be exhausted in May.
In contrast to 1995/96 (October-September), the bulk of Russian sunseeds from the last crop were exported in October-December, with the peak in November.
Mediterranean countries remain the major buyers.
In October 1996-February 1997, Turkey led the buying, with 191,700 tonnes.

However, Russia's sunseed exports to Mediterranean countries have declined year-on-year due to increased shipments to the Baltic and the North Sea countries, particularly to the Netherlands (178,700 tonnes in October 1996-February 1997) and Germany (53,900 tonnes over the same period).
On the domestic market, offered quantities are getting smaller and costlier.
Domestic sunseeds are currently offered at about one million roubles per tonne FCA including a 10 percent value-added tax. TABLE 1. DECLARED OILSEEDS EXPORTS INSPECTED BY THE STATE
